Re Alternatives, The Desert Protective Council agrees with the obvious fact that closing all Department of Interior lands to URV use would be the best alternative in terms of protecting the lands, but the sharp issue with the statement that "Closure to URV yould constitute an action inconsistent with the Department's responsibility to maintain cartain of its lands for the enjoyment and importation of the general public."
Closure to URV "ould not constitute closure to the "General Public" but rather provide equally for it on the public lands.
However, since Fundative Order 116'4 provides for controlled use of Wenth Public Lands, the Louert Protective Council will address itself to the necessity of full and complete departmental implementation of the order, without equivocation or degredation.
The Desert Protective Council questions the degree of protection in "sufficiently protected" and wonders what will constitute "significant adverse environmental impact or cause irreversible damage to existing ecological balances" and questions "rehabilitation of the land". Too often litter control is confused with rehabilitation.
REMABILITATION OF THE DESERT, THE PRIME TARGET OF ORV USE, CANNOT BE ACCUMPLISHED IN THE TIME OF MAN.
Nothing short of full and complete implementation of 11644 will do. The public, and the survival of quality, demands it. The Desert Protective Council concurs with the Sierra Club's frank assessment:
The operation of CRV's should be presumed to be detrimental to all areas and should accordingly be prohibited on all public lands unless proven otherwise by competent, is partial investigators."
